newsitem.title: FRANCE: Austrian police accused of ill-treatment.
newsitem.headline: Austrian police accused of ill-treatment.

text.p: The European Committee for the Prevention of Torture asked Austria on Thursday to investigate complaints that police had submitted detainees to ill-treatment akin to torture.

The Strasbourg-based committee said in a report on its visit to Austria in September-October 1994 that detainees at Vienna's Security Bureau and at some police stations reported being given electrical shocks.
Some complained they were made to choke with a plastic bag wrapped over their head, and were threatened with having their heads plunged into a bathtub.
The committee asked Vienna to set up an independent body to probe the charges. In comments attached to the report, the Austrian government said it was studying setting up the body.

The committee was created in 1987 under the European Convention for the Prevention of Torture which binds 30 of the 39 members of the Council of Europe, a body monitoring democracy and human rights based in the eastern French town of Strasbourg.
